title: He frowned when the blind man came
translation: He frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him. What would make you know? Perhaps he would grow pure, or take heed and profit by the reminder. As for the one who thinks himself self-sufficient…
body: Ibn Kathir: the Prophet frowned at the blind **Ibn Umm Maktum** while courting a Quraysh leader. Some Shia scholars (al-Murtada, **Tabataba’i**) refer it to an Umayyad man instead. James 2 rebukes **favouring the rich**; Luther faulted James on justification yet praised it for “vigorously promulgating **the law of God**”.
question: In verse 1, who frowns: the Prophet (Sunni exegetes) or an Umayyad man (some Shia scholars)? What does the wording support?
source_label: Ibn Kathir on 80:1-16 · Tabataba’i, al-Mizan · Luther, Preface to James
reading: Luther’s Works, vol. 35: Word and Sacrament I (prefaces to the New Testament)
